messages:
maria-support: Customer reported a sudden jump in p95 for /v1/chat this morning. They gave three request IDs seen during the spike: rq_xyz001, rq_xyz002, rq_xyz003. Asking for a focused repro pack so we can replay.

ashley-eng: Got it. Need a minimal repro pack — sample prompts, per-request token estimates, concurrency schedule, and any curl/HARs. If they can set an X-Client-Request-ID header we can tie traces back.

kevin-cust: We can add that header. Traffic pattern: steady ramp over 4 minutes, peak ~70 concurrent connections, short bursts at 60s and 180s. Typical message is our product preface + user payload, ~130 input tokens, requesting max_tokens=90. I'll attach a 10-row prompt CSV and one HAR from a representative client.

ashley-eng: Perfect. Please include the exact request bodies (or a representative promptset) and indicate whether clients used streaming. Example curl to use for replays:

ashley-eng: ```bash
curl "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Client-Request-ID: r_replay_01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are concise."},{"role":"user","content":"<PROMPT>"}],"max_tokens":90}'
```

ashley-eng: For load shape a simple vegeta targets file (one line per target with Authorization & X-Client-Request-ID) and this command should approximate the customer's ramp:

ashley-eng: ```bash
# create targets.txt with repeated lines
vegeta attack -rate=70 -connections=70 -duration=4m -targets=targets.txt | vegeta report
```

maria-support: Uploaded HAR and promptset to the support ticket. Promptset: 10 samples, median input tokens 132, median output ~68. Concurrency buckets they observed: [10,30,50,70,50,30] each 40s. Time window: 2026-03-13T14:12:00Z - 2026-03-13T14:20:00Z.

sam-sre: Checklist for the replay pack we will run in staging:
- HAR + curl conversions
- promptset CSV and token counts
- vegeta targets (with unique X-Client-Request-ID values)
- three sample client tcpdumps if available
- customer request IDs to look up traces (rq_xyz001,rq_xyz002,rq_xyz003)
- exact timezone / time window (included)

sam-sre: I will try to pull trace spans for the provided request IDs; if tracing is enabled we should see per-stage latencies and kernel timings.

ashley-eng: I'll perform an initial controlled replay this afternoon with the supplied promptset and concurrency schedule. Plan:
1) run 3 independent replays with identical targets
2) collect p50/p95/p99 and token-level latency breakdowns
3) capture runtime diagnostic bundle if p95 reproduces

ashley-eng: To collect the runtime diag bundle once we have suspect request IDs run internal diag tooling (example):

ashley-eng: ```bash
redwood-internal diag collect --ids rq_xyz001,rq_xyz002 --output diag-rqxyz.tar.gz
aws s3 cp diag-rqxyz.tar.gz s3://redwood-diags/1768003333/
```

ops-bot: diag job scheduled (job_id: diag-1768003333). Will post S3 link when upload completes.

kevin-cust: Thanks team. I'll drop the other two HARs and a tcpdump into the ticket link now. We ran clients from three regions so included region tags in the HAR filenames.

maria-support: Assigning to @ashley-eng and @sam-sre to lead the replay and trace collection. Kevin, please make sure the HARs contain full request headers so we can verify client-side retries/backs-off. :thumbsup:
